tasks.objective: Pin down the symptom onset timestamp and blast radius. Using query_logs and query_metrics, determine: (1) exact time payment-service error rate left baseline and whether ledger-write failures began simultaneously or earlier/later, (2) the precise error signatures/exception types on ledger write failures (validation error on new entry type? DB constraint violation? timeout? downstream 5xx?), (3) which other services show degradation in the same window (ledger-service, mandate/kyc service, DB/queue, auth), (4) whether there is any upstream latency/saturation trend on the ledger database or its host before 15:00Z. Report per-signal timestamps.
tasks.answer: payment-service error rate left baseline exactly at the 15:00Z bucket (0.18% at 14:55Z → 61.52% at 15:00Z). The ledger-write failures are NOT a validation/constraint/timeout error — they are disk-full failures ("No space left on device") caused by the ledger-db host running out of disk; ledger-db had already been warning on rising disk usage from 13:10Z (90%), 14:15Z (95%), 14:48Z (98%), and DB-level PANICs began 15:01:01Z. So the symptom is simultaneous (both at ~15:00–15:01Z) but the underlying host saturation started hours earlier — well before 15:00Z and before the v6.0.0 release window, which is inconsistent with the reported "new ledger entry type" theory.

tasks.objective: Map what changed around the incident window across ALL services. tasks.answer: Across ALL services between 12:00–16:59Z the only recorded change is a single deployment: payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46:00Z (new UPI mandate flow, new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD), already rolled back at 15:12:00Z. No config/flag changes anywhere, and nothing deployed on ledger-db or other shared infrastructure in that window. payment-service writes to the SHARED ledger-db (also used by order-, portfolio- and settlement-service) and produces to the shared kafka topic; there is no separate ledger-service. So v6.0.0 is the only deployment change, but the reported "ledger write failures" occur on shared infrastructure whose other consumers could also be affected — no telemetry/metrics were inspected here since that was out of this task's scope.

tasks.objective: Correlate the change timeline from task b against the exact onset time and error signature from task a, and test the competing hypotheses: (i) v6.0.0's new mandate/ledger entry type is rejected or mishandled downstream (rollback expected to fix), (ii) a change to ledger-service or shared infra in the same window is the real fault and rolling back payment-service will NOT fix it, (iii) saturation/backlog unrelated to deployment. tasks.answer: Evidence supports hypothesis (ii)/(iii) — ledger-db shared-infra disk exhaustion (WAL retained by the inactive 'analytics_cdc' replication slot, disk 90% at 13:10Z → 98% at 14:48Z, hard 'No space left on device' PANICs from 15:01Z) is the fault, strength HIGH for mechanism. Hypothesis (i) is CONTRADICTED: the error is a disk-full write failure, not a validation/constraint error on the new MANDATE_HOLD entry type, and disk pressure pre-dated the 14:46Z v6.0.0 deploy by ~1.5-2h. Falsifiable prediction: if rolling back payment-service were the fix, payment error rate should have fallen after 15:12:00Z; the evidence (F1) shows it stayed ~60% through 16:55Z, so the rollback will NOT remediate — the fix is on ledger-db (drop the retaining replication slot / free disk).

critiques.summary: H2 (ledger-db disk exhaustion from the inactive analytics_cdc replication slot) is well grounded on the mechanism: F3 establishes WAL retention by the slot from 13:02Z with disk 90%→98% (13:10Z→14:48Z), F4 establishes hard disk-full PANICs at 15:01Z, F2 establishes the single error signature as 'could not extend file: No space left on device' (not a validation error), and F12/F17 show the closest precedent (HIST-114) was fixed by dropping a slot, not by app rollback. Temporal order is sound: saturation onset ~13:02-13:10Z precedes payment onset 15:00Z and DB failure 15:01Z, and both precede/postdate the 14:46Z deploy in a way that falsifies the release-as-origin hypotheses (H1, H6). The separation from H5 (same origin, different accounting of which consumer filled the disk) is a secondary detail, not a different-origin ambiguity, so this is not 'inconclusive'. However two blocking-evidence gaps remain: (1) the claim that the slot is the dominant/only filler rests on an ASSUMPTION — the disk_used_pct time series was never successfully retrieved (tc-012 FAILED) and no WAL/slot retention size was quantified; (2) the shared-infra scope claim (H2 explains effects beyond payment-service) is asserted but the other three writers to shared ledger-db (order/portfolio/settlement) were never checked — if only payment-service failed, a payment-specific origin revives and could outrank H2. The post-rollback persistence (the decisive discriminator vs H1/H6) is also only second-hand from F1 and needs independent re-query. Confidence capped at 0.62.

challenges.issue: The load-bearing assumption that the analytics_cdc slot is the dominant/only consumer of disk space is NOT verified. disk_used_pct time series queries failed (tc-012 FAILED not_found), so the 'slot alone accounts for the fill' step is an inference from WARN threshold logs only, not a measured trajectory. The alternative under H5 (aggregate multi-writer capacity pressure) is not excluded by any retrieved data.

Scope is unproven. H2 predicts ALL writers to shared ledger-db should fail, but order-service / portfolio-service / settlement-service error rates in 15:00-16:59Z were never queried. If only payment-service failed, a payment-specific cause revives and the 'shared-infra' causal step (F2,F4 -> all writers fail) is broken.

The single most decisive discriminator vs H1/H6 — error rate persisting ~60% after the 15:12Z rollback — is only cited second-hand from F1 and was not independently re-queried. If it actually recovered promptly post-rollback, H6 (release pushed near-full disk over) regains support.

H5 is treated as a competing hypothesis but shares the same origin (ledger-db disk saturation) as H2, differing only in which consumer accounts for the fill. It should be merged/labelled as a secondary-detail variant, not ranked as a distinct-origin alternative.

The trigger/activation of the slot retaining WAL at 13:02Z is unexplained; no change event exists at 13:02Z (F8 zero config changes). This is consistent with chronic infra but leaves the 'repeatedly starting ~13:02Z' phrasing in the causal chain unverified as to why it started then.

critiques.summary: Round-1 blockers are now resolved. (1) Scope/blast radius: F31/F32/F33 (T5) confirm order-service and settlement-service — which never ran v6.0.0 — degraded at the same 15:00Z onset, order-service logging the identical 'No space left on device' signature. Three of four shared-ledger-db writers broke together, so the shared-infra causal step is established, not assumed. (2) Disk trajectory: F21/F22/F23 (T4) give the direct disk_used_pct ramp (86.57%@12:30Z → 100%@15:00Z, smooth, ~1%/6min, no step at the 14:46Z deploy, pinned at 100% through 16:54Z), replacing the earlier log-threshold-only proxy. (3) Decisive falsifier: F19/F20 (T4) independently confirm error_rate held ~60% (mean 62.29%) through 16:55Z after the 15:12Z rollback, on complete metrics (missing_points 0) — killing H1 and H6. Temporal order is sound (saturation 13:02–13:10Z precedes payment onset 15:00Z and DB PANICs 15:01Z, and precedes the 14:46Z deploy). H2 vs H5 name the SAME origin (ledger-db disk reaching capacity) and differ only in apportionment of the fill, so that residual uncertainty is a confidence cap, not an inconclusive split or a blocking gap. Remaining minor gaps: the ~13:02Z slot activation has no recorded trigger, no 2026-06-01 cleanup/recovery record exists, portfolio-service's immunity is unexplained, and whether portfolio-service's writes were affected at DB level. None of these could plausibly displace the top hypothesis or change the fix (free ledger-db disk / drop the retaining slot, not rollback). Accept with a modest cap for the unmeasured apportionment and unrecorded remediation event.

challenges.issue: The load-bearing claim that the analytics_cdc slot is the DOMINANT filler remains an assumption — WAL/slot retention size and its share of ledger-db disk were never measured, and the ~13:02Z activation of the slot has no recorded trigger (F25–F29, gaps). This is a secondary-detail uncertainty that H5 already accounts for identically, so it bounds confidence but does not change the origin or fix.

Mechanism is corroborated only by precedent (HIST-114, F12/F17/F28/F30); no 2026-06-01 slot-drop/WAL-cleanup record exists (F29) and disk stayed pinned at 100% with no observed recovery through 16:54Z (F23). The forward-looking mechanism is therefore plausible but not directly observed this incident.

Blast radius is 3 of 4 shared writers: portfolio-service stayed flat (~0.21% error_rate, zero ERROR logs, flat db_pool F34/F35). The mechanism making it immune is unexplained; if portfolio-service also writes to the same WAL-generating path, the 'all writes failed' phrasing overstates universality (though the disk-full DB-level fault is still clearly shared infra).

H5 is not a distinct origin — it names the same ledger-db capacity ceiling and differs only in apportionment of the fill. Listing it as a separate ranked hypothesis risks implying two candidate fixes when there is one.
